from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication: Stretching Space", [
            "Scalars stretch or shrink vectors.",
            "They change length, maintaining orientation.",
            "Negative scalars reverse the direction."

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Basis vectors i and j are building blocks.", "Any 2D vector is their linear combination.", "They define the coordinate grid."]
        self.setup_layout("Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid Background - Switched from ImageMobject to SVGMobject as it is an SVG file
        grid_bg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        self.place_in_area(grid_bg, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.add(grid_bg)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#00FFFF")
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Placing at grid coordinates using axes.c2p
        i_vec = axes.c2p(1, 0)
        j_vec = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        
        i_hat.shift(origin - i_hat.get_start())
        j_hat.shift(origin - j_hat.get_start())
        
        self.play(Create(i_hat))
        self.play(Create(j_hat))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v} = 3\\hat{i} + 2\\hat{j}", color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "C4", scale_factor=0.75)
        
        v_vector = Vector(axes.c2p(3, 2) - origin, color="#FF4500")
        v_vector.shift(origin - v_vector.get_start())
        
        self.play(Create(v_vector))
        self.play(Write(v_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        grid_lines = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3]).scale(0.6).move_to(axes.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_lines))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Vectors combine instructions for spatial transformation.", 
            "They form the basis for coordinate systems.", 
            "Linear algebra enables complex visual movement."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        airplane = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/airplane.svg", color=WHITE)
        satellite = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg", color=WHITE)
        camera = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg", color=WHITE)
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg", color="#FFD700")

        assets_group = VGroup(airplane, satellite, camera).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(assets_group, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Robot for line 2
        self.place_at_grid(robot, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        robot.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(assets_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(robot))
        self.play(Indicate(robot))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(assets_group), FadeOut(robot))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Movement)
sections.content: Introduce vectors as directed line segments in 2D space defined by magnitude and direction. Explain how a vector acts as an 'instruction' to move from an origin (0,0) to a coordinate (x,y).
sections.example: Visualize a robotic turtle starting at the origin; a vector [3, 2] is the specific command for it to walk 3 units right and 2 units up.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Demonstrate that adding vectors corresponds to sequential movements. Graphically, this is shown by placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first.
sections.example: The turtle walks [3, 2] (first vector), then walks [1, 4] (second vector). The 'resultant' vector is the straight path from the origin to the turtle's final position [4, 6].

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching Space
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar (number) changes its length but keeps its orientation (unless negative). This 'stretches' or 'shrinks' the vector graphically.
sections.example: If a bird is flying along vector [1, 1], multiplying by 2 results in [2, 2], visually doubling the length of the flight path while maintaining the same diagonal angle.

sections.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
sections.content: Define 'i' [1, 0] and 'j' [0, 1] as the unit basis vectors. Explain that any 2D vector is simply a linear combination: x*i + y*j.
sections.example: Think of [3, 2] as a recipe: 3 portions of 'horizontal unit move' plus 2 portions of 'vertical unit move'. This shows why these two vectors are the 'grid' for all 2D space.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap that linear algebra is the study of how these spatial instructions combine to transform the entire grid, setting the stage for matrices and transformations.
sections.example: Summarize how simple vectors (arrows) form the coordinate system used in every video game to animate characters moving across a screen.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The axes object is centered too low and right, causing an imbalance in the visual composition. Fix: Line 58: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2) (line=58, object=axes)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'x = 3' label is positioned too far from the base of the vector, creating visual detachment. Fix: Line 80: self.place_at_grid(x_label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9) (line=80, object=x_label)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed x_label positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'y = 2' label occupies a grid cell that risks obscuring the vertical extent of the vector. Fix: Line 83: self.place_at_grid(y_label, 'C6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=83, object=y_label)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed y_label positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The axes object occupies too much horizontal space, pushing into the right margin and potentially crowding the center area. Fix: Line 53: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=53, object=axes)
issues.resolution_note: Updated axes positioning to 'B3'-'F6' with scale 0.6.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Lack of visual distinction between the lecture text and the animated workspace causes potential clutter. Fix: Line 10: self.place_in_area(lecture_group, 'A1', 'F2', scale_factor=0.9) (line=10, object=lecture_lines)
issues.resolution_note: Positioning of the entire lecture text group is already handled by to_edge in base class setup_layout. Added note that layout constraint is satisfied.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The current origin of the coordinate system is not aligned with the visual grid's center of gravity. Fix: Line 53: self.place_at_grid(origin_point, 'D4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=53, object=origin_point)
issues.resolution_note: Added origin marker at grid 'D4'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Vector animations at C4 obscure the central grid and lack visual separation from lecture text. Fix: Line 57: self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=57, object=vec)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed grid position to C5 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Overwriting vectors at the same coordinate (C4) causes visual clutter and loss of state history. Fix: Line 68: self.place_at_grid(new_vec, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=68, object=new_vec)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed grid position to D5 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The negative vector animation at C4 is cramped; shifting creates better negative space balance. Fix: Line 75: self.place_at_grid(neg_vec, 'E5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=75, object=neg_vec)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed grid position to E5 as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The axes object occupies the full width, causing animations to obstruct the lecture text on the left. Fix: Line 51: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=51, object=axes)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed axes positioning to B3-F6.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The vector label 'v_label' is too high and far from the animation area, creating visual disconnect. Fix: Line 74: self.place_at_grid(v_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=74, object=v_label)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Poor grid utilization leads to excessive empty space and prevents logical grouping of formula to axes. Fix: Line 74: self.place_at_grid(v_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.75) (line=74, object=v_label)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The vector animation overlaps with the lecture text, reducing readability of both. Fix: self.place_in_area(vector_animation, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=1, object=Vector diagram)
